clue.text: Boodle's mark

parts.note: the B that opens Boodle, split off as it stands
oodles means lots, so a single oodle is a lot; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A distinguishing sign belonging to Boodle's, the old London gentlemen's club.
explanation.walkthrough: Split Boodle's as B + oodle's: an oodle, singular of oodles, is a lot, so B + LOT, with 's as 'is', gives a mark. Boodle's is a St James's club in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A blot is a stain or smudge, one kind of mark on a surface.

clue.text: Nice day, on reflection, for correspondent

parts.note: Nice is the French city, and in French a day is jour

indicators.note: on reflection, the little word on is mirrored so it reads backwards

explanation.surface: Someone muses that a pleasant day was in fact ideal for a letter-writer or reporter.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French Riviera city, not the adjective: its language turns day into JOUR. 'On reflection' turns ON into NO.
explanation.definitionFit: Journo is informal slang for a journalist, and a newspaper correspondent is one such reporter.

clue.text: Brambles not right as an environment for raising wildlife and fools

indicators.note: an environment surrounds what lives in it, so the trimmed brambles wrap round the other piece
not tells us to leave the R for right out of the word brambles
in a down clue, raising lifts the word upwards so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a zoo is a place full of wildlife, so wildlife stands for zoo

explanation.surface: Thorny hedges make a good habitat for rearing animals, and also for trapping the gullible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raising' reverses in this down clue, and 'as an environment for' wraps BAMBLES (brambles minus R, signalled by 'not') around the result. 'Wildlife' looks like the subject; it stands for the zoo.
explanation.definitionFit: To bamboozle someone is to trick or deceive them, the same as making a fool of them.

clue.text: Religious people gathering shells, essentially as ornaments

indicators.note: gathering means taking something in, so the outer word holds the inner piece

parts.note: Jews are followers of the Jewish religion

indicators.note: essentially points to the essence or core of the word shells, its middle letters

explanation.surface: Worshippers collect seashells to use as decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Essentially' takes the core of shells and 'gathering' has the religious people hold it; 'shells' looks like the thing collected but only its centre is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Jewels are gems worn as personal adornment, so they are ornaments.

clue.text: Group competently curbs rising disorder

indicators.note: curbs means holds in, so the first word restrains the other inside it

parts.note: ably means competently, with skill

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising makes the word read from bottom to top

parts.note: a mess is a state of disorder

explanation.surface: A collective efficiently suppresses a growing uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' reads disorder's synonym upwards in this down clue, and 'curbs' holds it in; 'rising disorder' looks like a revolt but splits into indicator and fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An assembly is a gathering of people, such as a legislature or school gathering, so a group.

clue.text: Being old, will droop

definitions.meaning: ... is the archaic second-person form of will, as in 'thou ...'
to sag or droop, like a flower without water

explanation.surface: Getting on in years, a person or plant is bound to sag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being old' flags an archaic form: 'thou wilt' is old English for 'you will'. WILT is also a Tom Sharpe novel, one of the puzzle's hidden theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Plants that lack water wilt, their stems and leaves sagging limply.

clue.text: Dine out on little money? That's vulgar

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits on top of the second
out suggests the letters of dine are put out of order

parts.note: a cent is a coin of small value, a little money

explanation.surface: Someone sneers at eating in a restaurant on a tiny budget as tasteless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' scrambles 'Dine' and 'on' stacks it above the coin in this down clue; 'Dine out' reads as a single phrase but splits into fodder and signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indecent offends against good taste or decency, which is what vulgar describes.

clue.text: Working majority of 13 across or 3

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked over into a new arrangement
majority of means most of the word, its first four of seven letters, dropping the rest

parts.note: the answer to 13 across, a word meaning turbulent

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asking for a slim working majority, or simply the number three.
explanation.walkthrough: Most of 13 across is RIOT; 'Working' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three, such as three musicians playing together.

clue.text: Powder room makes sleepyhead somehow appear dishevelled

parts.note: a powder room is a polite name for a toilet, a loo

indicators.note: somehow suggests these letters come together in some other order

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of sleepy

explanation.surface: A sleepy person staggers into the ladies' and sees their bedraggled reflection.
explanation.walkthrough: Powder room is a genteel euphemism for the toilet. The letters of 'makes' are reordered into KAMES; sleepyhead is read as the head of sleepy.
explanation.definitionFit: To look a mess is to appear untidy, the idiom for being scruffy or dishevelled.

clue.text: Essential sign in heart oddly ignored

indicators.note: with the odd letters ignored, only the even-placed letters of these words are kept

explanation.surface: A vital symbol inside a heart has been mysteriously overlooked.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of 'sign in heart' leaves the 2nd, 4th, 6th, 8th and 10th: I, N, N, E, R.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner part of something is its core, what is essential to it, as in inner meaning.

clue.text: Pound discovered in a bath robe

indicators.note: discovered means found or uncovered within the following words

explanation.surface: A pound coin turns up in the pocket of a dressing gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pound' looks like money, but it is the verb: to beat.
explanation.definitionFit: To pound and to throb both describe a heavy rhythmic beat, as of a heart or a headache.

clue.text: Helen and Ruth unclothed by champion of alternative medicine

indicators.note: by means beside, so the champion is placed next to the trimmed names
unclothed strips the outer layer off each name, leaving its inner letters

parts.note: a champion is a hero, someone who fights for a cause

explanation.surface: Two women are undressed by a man promoting alternative therapies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unclothed' strips each name to its middle: HELEN gives ELE and RUTH gives UT; 'by' sets HERO beside them.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleuthero, also called Siberian ginseng, is a herbal root sold as a natural remedy, a staple of alternative healing.

clue.text: Turbulent river in Europe, as far as the Guardian is concerned

parts.note: rio is the word for river in Spain and Portugal

parts.words: as far as the Guardian is concerned
parts.note: the newspaper speaks of itself as us, so in its view something is 'to us'

explanation.surface: A fierce European river is described from the newspaper's own point of view.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian is the paper that printed this puzzle, so its 'to us' is the house we.
explanation.definitionFit: Riotous means wild and disorderly, close to turbulent in describing unruly conditions.

clue.text: Up or down detector

indicators.note: up or down says the word reads the same whichever way it runs in this down clue

parts.note: a detection system, and the word itself reads the same both ways

explanation.surface: An instrument that senses things moving up or down.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer reads identically from top or bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Radar is a system that uses radio waves to locate aircraft and ships, a detection device.

clue.text: Clothes on fire?

parts.note: jackets of a certain style, read playfully as things that are aflame

explanation.surface: An alarmed question about garments ablaze.
explanation.walkthrough: Blazers are sporting jackets, but read literally as 'things that blaze' they are on fire.
explanation.definitionFit: A blazer is a light jacket, often in school or club colours, so a garment; things that blaze are burning.

clue.text: Perhaps too bad a mark

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters are spoiled and turned into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A teacher thinks a low grade may be too harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Too bad' reads as a phrase; 'too' is part of the anagram and 'bad' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostrophe is a punctuation mark, used for possession or omitted letters.

clue.text: See 24
Live or die, that's come out nicely

indicators.note: come out means the letters named leave the word die

parts.note: that is, abbreviated i.e.
nicely means well, in a good way

explanation.surface: Someone insists that, whether you live or die, things turned out fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is i.e. (that is), which comes out of DIE to leave D, followed by WELL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dwell somewhere is to reside or live there.

clue.text: Showing Europe's upset about vote

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece
upset means knocked over, so the letters of Europe's are turned into a new order

parts.note: a voter marks the ballot paper with a cross, X

explanation.surface: A continent is in turmoil over a ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' rearranges EUROPES (apostrophe dropped), and 'about' puts it round X.
explanation.definitionFit: Exposure is the act of revealing, the state of being shown or displayed publicly.

clue.text: A city in Tanganyika, doesn't matter which

parts.note: NY is New York, the city; the answer also sits hidden in Tanganyika, a deliberate second route rather than a coincidence

explanation.surface: A town somewhere in Tanganyika will do; any one at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A second route also works: A followed by NY, short for New York, the city. Tanganyika is the former name of mainland Tanzania.
explanation.definitionFit: Any used of a choice means whichever one, no particular one being required.

clue.text: Enough said, every now and then, on match

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second
every now and then means taking only some of the letters at regular gaps

parts.note: to match two things is to equate them

explanation.surface: Enough has been said, now and again, about a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every now and then' keeps the even letters of 'said', and 'on' sets them above the next piece in this down clue. 'Match' looks like a game but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Adequate means sufficient for the need, just as enough does.

clue.text: Portsmouth & Co

parts.note: read as a port's mouth and others like it: a port, and mouths in the plural

explanation.surface: A firm name, or the English naval city and its companions.
explanation.walkthrough: Split Portsmouth into port + mouth: Ostia was the port of ancient Rome, and in anatomy ostia (plural of ostium) are mouth-like openings. Portsmouth is an English naval port.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostia was the harbour of ancient Rome, and its name comes from the Latin for mouths, as at a river's estuary.

clue.text: East German in mature comeback

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the word for mature

parts.note: ripe means mature, ready to eat
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: A veteran from the old East Germany makes a return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' looks like a person; it is the German word for east, OST.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick sharp reply, a verbal comeback.

clue.text: Terribly quaint and ultimately obsolete

indicators.note: terribly suggests the word quaint is badly mangled into a new order
ultimately points at the final letter of obsolete

explanation.surface: A description of an antique: hopelessly old-fashioned and out of date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terribly' rearranges QUAINT into ANTIQU, and 'ultimately' adds E, the last letter of obsolete; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An antique is an old object from an earlier era, and the clue describes such a thing as quaint and outdated.

clue.text: In the Mao revolution

indicators.note: a revolution turns things around, so these letters are turned into another order

explanation.surface: Taking part in the Chinese Communist uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolution' rearranges THE MAO; 'In' looks like a preposition but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: If someone is in, they are at home rather than out.

clue.text: Source of stone that is sought by hunters

definitions.meaning: a pit from which building stone is dug
a hunter's ... is the animal being chased

explanation.surface: A rock pit where hunters go looking for something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word has two senses: an open pit for extracting stone, and prey being pursued.

clue.text: Is it best to have laid out a stall that's disgusting?

indicators.note: laid out suggests the letters are spread out and rearranged

parts.note: ugh is the exclamation for something disgusting

explanation.surface: A shopper wonders whether arranging a market stall in such a revolting way is wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Laid out' rearranges A STALL; the definition plays on the saying 'he who laughs last laughs best'.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says the one who laughs last laughs longest and best, so the final triumph is the one worth having.

clue.text: No portrait of elaborate lap dances

indicators.note: elaborate means worked over in detail, so these letters are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: No picture was painted of the fancy routines in a strip club.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer spans this light and 16. 'No portrait' plays on page orientation: a landscape page is wide, a portrait one tall.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape painting shows scenery, not a person, so it is the opposite of a portrait; the terms also name page layouts.

clue.text: They say thin is right

indicators.note: they say marks a word spoken out loud and heard, not written

parts.note: lean means thin, slender

explanation.surface: People claim that being slim is correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They say' turns LEAN into its sound-alike. A lien is a legal claim.
explanation.definitionFit: A lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid.

clue.text: The hapless are to speak

indicators.note: hapless means unlucky, so these words suffer a mishap and are rearranged

explanation.surface: The unfortunate ones are going to give a talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hapless' rearranges ARE TO; 'to' looks part of the definition but belongs to the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a formal speech, so to speak at length.

clue.text: Brew beer, only half jug

indicators.note: only half means just the second half of each word, its last two letters

explanation.surface: A homebrewer makes beer but fills just part of a pitcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only half' keeps the back half of each word: EW from brew and ER from beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A ewer is a large water jug, often with a wide spout.

clue.text: One's art without frames, extremely versatile and daring

indicators.note: taking away the frames of each word strips its first and last letters
extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters of versatile

explanation.surface: Unframed pictures show a person's art to be very adaptable and bold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without frames' leaves NE from One's and R from art; 'extremely' gives VE, the ends of versatile.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve is boldness or courage, as in having the nerve to do something risky.

clue.text: Writer's book contains clever mixed metaphors

indicators.note: contains means the book holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: a tome is a large book
sharp means clever, quick-witted

explanation.surface: An author's volume is full of muddled figurative language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixed metaphors' also rearranges into the answer, a second route. Tom Sharpe was an English comic novelist whose titles (Wilt, Riotous Assembly) hide in this grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Sharpe was a British author of farcical novels such as Porterhouse Blue.
